scale.common: 0 unusable/absent; 2 severely compromised; 4 weak prototype; 5 functional mixed prototype; 6 promising but conspicuously limited; 7 solid indie/vertical-slice quality; 8 polished release quality; 9 exceptional; 10 reference-leading. Ratings assess only actual observed coverage.
scale.gameplay: Combat, movement, encounter decisions and reward loop.
scale.presentation: Art direction, environment, animation and audiovisual polish (audio not assessed here).
scale.usability: Control discoverability, navigation and interaction workflow.
scale.readability: Legibility of threats, objectives, feedback and geometry.
scale.AAA-readiness: Observed distance to contemporary premium FPS production finish and breadth; not a claim about unseen content.

gameplay.reason: Optic kill, recovery resupply and visibly interruptible Warden create an understandable loop. Alternate archive approach works. Robot movement and repeated exposed holds feel basic; pressure overtook my navigation. Two deaths prevent evaluation of full loop.

presentation.reason: Strong restrained teal/amber identity, rainy reflective yard, coherent menu and mission composition. Very simple geometric robots, props and close-up surfaces reveal prototype scope. No audio judgment.

usability.reason: Controls are visible; precise receiver reach feedback and paused map help. Frequent low-cover/generator collisions interrupted movement; aim turn sensitivity took experimentation. Fresh reset is clear.

readability.reason: Orange optic, incoming-fire wedges, recovery announcements and named archives read well. Small distant threats and dense map/trace-like indicators are harder to parse; flat low cover sometimes hides route continuation. Small text is abundant.

AAA-readiness.reason: Coherent and promising vertical-slice shell, but simplified models, limited witnessed combat variation and prototype geometry remain well below premium FPS finish. Full mission, boss/jammer, extraction and robustness remain unverified.
